name: SAN MARINO

flag.title: San Marino
flag.note: White over sky-blue, coat of arms centred

lead: San Marino sits on a rocky mountain inside Italy. It is the world's oldest republic. Three stone towers stand on the peak. A stonemason named Marinus founded it in AD 301.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: San Marino sits on Monte Titano, a limestone mountain 749 m high. The whole country covers just 61 km². You could walk across it in a morning.
Oak and chestnut woods cover the slopes. The mountain catches clouds, so it is cooler and rainier than the plains.
animals: Peregrine falcons nest on the cliffs. They are San Marino's national bird. They are also the fastest animal on Earth, diving at over 300 km/h.
Red foxes, badgers, hedgehogs and martens live in the oak woods. Roe deer graze in the valleys.
culture: The Torta Tre Monti is a cake shaped like the three towers. Wafer layers hold hazelnut and cocoa cream. Piadina is a folded flatbread stuffed with prosciutto or cheese.
Every 3 September is national day. Teams in medieval costume hold a crossbow contest in an old stone quarry. In March, bonfires called focheracce glow in every castle district.
history: A stonemason named Marinus sailed from the island of Rab. He was running from cruel Roman rulers. Around AD 301, he built a chapel on Monte Titano and declared the land free.
His last words were 'I leave you free from both men.' He meant the Emperor and the Pope. Napoleon once offered to enlarge San Marino. The people said no.
wows: San Marino began in AD 301. That makes it over 1,700 years old.
The whole country is smaller than Florence, yet it has its own army.
Two Captains Regent lead the country together. They swap every six months.
In 1865, San Marino was among the first countries to end the death penalty.
Against England, San Marino scored after 8.3 seconds. It is the fastest international goal ever.
San Marino is tiny, but it is one of Europe's wealthiest countries per person.
Collectors around the world buy its stamps. Those sales help pay the country's bills.

myths.myth: Tiny countries never win Olympic medals
myths.fact: At the Tokyo Games, San Marino won Olympic medals. No smaller nation has ever won one.

myths.myth: San Marino is the smallest country in Europe
myths.fact: Two countries are smaller. Vatican City and Monaco would both fit inside San Marino.
